changes.title: AWS Parallel Computing Service now supports managed instance health checks
changes.detail: AWS Parallel Computing Service (AWS PCS) now supports instance health checks, which can find hardware faults and software problems on accelerated instances beyond what Amazon EC2 detects today. For example, a fault such as an uncorrectable GPU memory error can stop or slow every job on a compute node. Instead of losing the next job to the same bad GPU, AWS PCS can take the compute node out of scheduling and replace its instance with a new one. changes.title: AWS Parallel Computing Service now supports network topology-aware scheduling
changes.detail: AWS Parallel Computing Service (AWS PCS) now supports network topology-aware scheduling, which can place the nodes of each multi-node Slurm job as close together as possible in the Amazon EC2 network. For example, a tightly-coupled MPI simulation or distributed training job exchanges data between its nodes many times per step, so nodes that are many network hops apart can slow every step. Instead of every node in a queue looking equally close to Slurm, AWS PCS can tell Slurm where each compute node sits in the network, so the job can run on nodes fewer hops apart.
